findings.evidence: apps/jobs-runtime/src/child.ts close(): after its two 5000ms races, the last live-child branch calls child.kill(SIGTERM) and awaits done without any further bound. apps/jobs-runtime/src/worker.ts:161 installs a SIGTERM listener that runs asynchronous stop().
findings.refutation: Normal cooperative workers will close, and Windows terminates SIGTERM differently. The supported Linux/WSL topology can retain a process whose application handler blocks the event loop or whose shutdown never resolves; its signal listener does not guarantee exit, so the parent can wait forever. A new native guardian can clean engine ownership without forcing this application child to exit.
findings.suggestion: Bound final application-child termination and escalate through its actual ChildProcess handle; prove a noncooperative child cannot hang supervisor shutdown/restart.
